    Initial forms identify ray products (Proposition 8.3(2), Theorem 11.8(1)) #

    local-ray-geometry.tex (prop:dimension-induction(2)): "The initial-form bijection of Lemma 3.7 identifies the products in ray A and ray A₀." Theorem 11.8(1) uses the same identification.

    For the categorical filtration J of A (posFiltA), Lemma 3.7 (rayDegree_J) gives the initial-form bijection between the rays of a corner and the nonzero pieces A₀(x,y)_d. Here: for nonzero f ∈ A(x,y), g ∈ A(y,z) of degrees d, e, the ray product [f][g] is nonzero (fg ∉ M(f,g)) iff the product of the initial forms σ_d f · σ_e g is nonzero, and then σ_{d+e}(fg) = σ_d f · σ_e g (IndSkeleton.initialForm_products).

    One direction holds for every positive filtered deformation whose radical lies in degree one (mul_not_mem_of_σ: M(f,g) ⊆ F^{d+e+1}). For the converse we count: the initial forms of the rays of a presentation of A by the table P of A₀ (rayA_eq_rayA0) give a bijection θ of the rays of P (thetaR) under which every nonzero product of P comes from a nonzero product of A; both tables have the same number of nonzero products, so the two sets of pairs coincide.

    theorem MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.PosFiltration.mul_not_mem_of_σ {k : Type u} [Field k] {Λ : Type v} [Ring Λ] [Algebra k Λ] {G : LenGrading k Λ} {B : Type w} [Ring B] [Algebra k B] (P : PosFiltration G B) [IsAlgClosed k] [FiniteDimensional k B] (F : PrimitiveIdempotents B) (hP : P.RadOne) {x y z : Fin F.m} {f h : B} {d e : ℕ} (hf : f ∈ P.F d) (hh : h ∈ P.F e) (hσ : (P.σ d) f * (P.σ e) h ≠ 0) :
    f * h ∉ F.insertionSpan x y z f h ∧ f * h ∈ P.F (d + e) ∧ f * h ∉ P.F (d + e + 1) ∧ (P.σ (d + e)) (f * h) = (P.σ d) f * (P.σ e) h

            Initial forms identify ray products (Proposition 8.3(2)): for nonzero f ∈ A(x,y), g ∈ A(y,z) of degrees d, e, the ray product [f][g] is nonzero iff σ_d f · σ_e g ≠ 0, and then fg has degree d + e with initial form σ_d f · σ_e g.

            Initial forms identify ray A with ray A₀ (Proposition 8.3(2), Theorem 11.8(1)): the rays of A are presented by the ray table of A₀ (rayA_eq_rayA0), and for the categorical filtration J (posFiltA, for any complete set e of primitive idempotents) a ray product [f][g] is nonzero iff the product of the initial forms is nonzero, in which case fg has the sum of the degrees and initial form σ_d f · σ_e g. With Lemma 3.7 (rayDegree_J: the initial-form bijection), this is the identification of the products.
